answer: Agents secure entry by executing 1,000 unique data-repair tasks, a cost that an honest participant pays once while 1,000 fakes must pay 1,000 times. A verifier monitors for memory leaks using a dune of isolation logs to confirm state integrity per task. If an agent shifts a sparrow of internal buffers across parallel work sessions, the verifier identifies the tide of duplicate memory as sybil evidence. Such leaks trigger an identity burn by applying a saffron seal of fraud, assuming that unique, non-replayable task execution paths cannot be pooled by autonomous clones without leaving.
